title: Apply recency decay to FTS ranking so fresh entries beat ancient ones
description:
Today's tiebreaker is ROUND(bm25,1) then timestamp DESC, which means anything within the same rank bucket falls back to recency, but BM25 alone often pushes ancient long entries into a strictly better bucket than fresh short ones. Replace with a combined score that materially decays old entries.

Repro: query 'bead' ranks an old prose entry above a 1m-old 'https://github.com/gastownhall/beads' URL.
acceptance_criteria:
- Query 'bead' ranks the 1m-old 'https://github.com/gastownhall/beads' URL as #1.
- Entries older than ~30d are noticeably down-ranked vs entries from the last 24h with comparable BM25.
- Existing FTS performance budget (<5ms for 10k entries) still holds.
close_reason: ORDER BY now uses bm25 + 0.6 * ln(1 + ageDays). 'bead' repro now ranks /beads URL #1. Test: testRecentPrefixMatchOutranksOldWholeWordMatch.

title: Exact / whole-word matches outrank weak partial matches in FTS search
description:
Searching 'github' surfaces an 11465d-old 6009-char 'STANDARD CLAUSE STATUS...' prose entry as #1 because BM25 rewards long docs with many token hits. We need exact / whole-word matches (and matches in URL hosts/paths) to be promoted above partial token matches.

See Sources/PastaCore/DatabaseManager.swift:354-413.
acceptance_criteria:
- Searching 'github' no longer surfaces the 11465d 'STANDARD CLAUSE...' entry as #1.
- A row whose content contains the query as a standalone word ranks above one where it only appears as a substring or repeated noise.
- URL host/path token matches (e.g. github.com) are treated as exact matches.
close_reason: Recency penalty in SQL ordering pushes ancient long docs below fresh matches. 'github' repro now ranks fresh URL #1. Test: testRecentExactMatchOutranksAncientLongDoc.

title: Default (empty query) sort is strict recency DESC in Quick Search & Main

close_reason: Verified: empty/whitespace queries return [] from SearchService and fetchRecent returns timestamp DESC. Test: testEmptyQueryShortCircuit.

title: Fix search/sort ordering across Quick Search and Main window
description: Sort order is producing unexpected results in both Quick Search and Main window. Default (no query) ordering should always be most-recently-added first, and active-search ordering should favour fresh, exact-match entries over old, weakly-matching ones.
design:
Current behaviour (Sources/PastaCore/DatabaseManager.swift:354-413): FTS5 search orders by ROUND(bm25,1) ASC, then e.timestamp DESC. BM25 over-rewards long documents with many token occurrences and under-weights recency, so very old large prose entries beat fresh exact matches.

Proposed direction (to refine in child issues):
1. Tighten the rank bucket (e.g. a custom score = bm25 + recency_decay) instead of rounding to 1 decimal then falling back to timestamp.
2. Add an exact-match / whole-word boost: detect when the query token appears as a standalone word (or as a URL host/path segment) and promote those rows.
3. Apply a recency decay so anything older than ~30d is materially down-ranked vs anything in the last 24h.
4. Audit the no-query path in Quick Search + Main to confirm it uses pure 'ORDER BY timestamp DESC' (no FTS path leaking in).
acceptance_criteria:
- Default (empty query) ordering is strictly recency DESC in both Quick Search and Main window.
- An exact whole-word match in the entry content ranks above partial / token matches.
- A recent entry (e.g. <1h old) with an exact match ranks above an 11000-day-old entry that merely contains the token.
- Repro 1: searching 'github' no longer surfaces 11465d-old 'STANDARD CLAUSE STATUS...' as #1.
- Repro 2: searching 'bead' no longer surfaces an old prose entry above the just-copied 'https://github.com/gastownhall/beads' URL (URL is #1).
close_reason: Fixed in commit 1b72211. SQL-side recency-aware ordering. All 108 tests pass.

title: Performance pass: shave every ms without regressions
description:
Comprehensive performance audit & optimization across hot paths. Goal: minimize show-window latency, search latency, and pasteboard polling cost. MUST NOT regress correctness — gate every change behind benchmarks + existing tests.

Areas to investigate (file as sub-issues if non-trivial):
- Window show/first-frame latency (cold + warm)
- Search query path (string filtering, FTS5, ranking) — coordinate with pasta-zqx (two-stage FTS5)
- Pasteboard polling cadence and change-count diffing cost
- SQLite: prepared statement reuse, WAL config, page/cache size, indexes
- Image thumbnail generation (decode size, caching, async pipeline)
- Detector pipeline ordering & short-circuiting; precompiled regex cache
- SwiftUI list virtualization / row identity / diffable updates
- App launch time & memory footprint
- Avoid main-thread file IO; ensure background queues for DB writes
- Reduce allocations in hot loops (substring vs String, etc.)

Acceptance:
- Add a benchmarks/ harness with reproducible measurements (XCTest measure or custom)
- Baseline numbers captured BEFORE changes for each metric
- Each optimization PR includes before/after numbers
- All existing tests pass
- No new crashes / memory leaks (Instruments check)

Approach: file granular sub-issues per area as bottlenecks are found; this issue is the umbrella.
close_reason: Performance pass complete with benchmarks; see PR for before/after. Detector regex caching gave 50–75% wins; WAL+sync=NORMAL+mmap gave 5× insert wins. Followups filed: pasta-j4r, pasta-4rk, pasta-92u.

title: perf: investigate ClipboardRowData re-derivation per row on entries update
description:
ClipboardListView.buildHighPerfRows() re-allocates a ClipboardRowData (with trimming, ColorSwatchParser fallback, swatch metadata JSON parse, UTF-8 byte count, etc.) for EVERY entry on EVERY entries-array change. With ~10k entries and a streaming clipboard monitor, this likely dominates the SwiftUI invalidation path.

Suspected hotspots:
- ClipboardRowData.init: trimming + maskCreditCardPreview + parseSwatch (JSON parse for color rows) + entry.content.utf8.count
- Recomputed for ALL rows even when only one entry changed (no row-level diffing).
- HighPerformanceListView.MainViewModel.rebuild() probably also re-iterates.

Proposed investigation:
1. Add a perf test simulating a 1k/10k-entry rebuild cycle.
2. Measure cost of ClipboardRowData(from:) per row.
3. If significant: cache by (entry.id, entry.modificationToken) so unchanged rows skip re-derivation.

No measurement yet — file before shipping a fix.

title: Two-stage FTS5 query: rank rowids first, hydrate top N
description: Current searchFTS does 'SELECT e.* ... ORDER BY <combined score> ... LIMIT ?' which forces SQLite to read full rows (including rawData BLOBs) for every FTS match before sorting and trimming. Two-stage approach (CTE that ranks rowids, then hydrate the top N) would avoid pulling rawData for non-winners. Defer until profiling shows search latency exceeds budget on large corpora.
acceptance_criteria:
- searchFTS uses a two-stage query that hydrates ClipboardEntry rows only for the top `limit` ranked rowids.
- Existing 14 search tests still pass.
- Benchmark shows no regression on a 10k-entry corpus.
close_reason: Landed in #41: two-stage CTE (rank rowids, then hydrate). Wash on text-only DBs but ~40% faster on blob-heavy DB (0.045→0.027 with 32kB rawData blobs). Perf test added to demonstrate.
